sections.h2: What is Frederick, Maryland, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Frederick is the seat of Frederick County and the second-largest incorporated city in Maryland after Baltimore. It sits about 46 miles west of Baltimore and roughly 50 miles north of Washington, D.C., where Catoctin Mountain meets the Piedmont.

The city covers 24.56 square miles. The Monocacy River runs east of town, and Carroll Creek runs through it. The 2020 Census counted 78,171 people, up from 65,239 in 2010, a gain of 19.8% in ten years. That growth means plenty of newer subdivisions on the edges, and an older core downtown where the houses are far older than the rest of the housing stock.

sections.h2: What is Frederick's history, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Daniel Dulany laid out Frederick Town in 1745, and Frederick County was formed in 1748 with the town as its seat.

Schifferstadt, built in 1756, is described by Wikipedia as probably the oldest standing house in the city. In 1861 Frederick briefly served as Maryland's capital while the legislature debated secession, and in July 1864 the Battle of Monocacy was fought just southeast of town. The C&O Canal began operating and the B&O Frederick Branch was completed in 1831.

If you own a house in the center, its age can bring its own questions: older wiring, plaster, small closets, stone or brick foundations and the like. A buyer will price those in, and a cash buyer will usually look at the structure as is rather than ask you to modernize first.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers around Frederick?
sections.html:
Fort Detrick is the largest employer in Frederick County, with 10,827 employees in 2025, followed by the county school system. The list leans heavily toward federal, biomedical and public-sector jobs.

  • Fort Detrick (U.S. Army bioscience and communications): 10,827
  • Frederick County Board of Education: 7,433
  • Frederick Health: 3,360
  • Frederick County Government: 2,810
  • Leidos Biomedical Research: 2,370
  • Frederick Community College: 1,369
  • Frederick City Government: 977
  • AstraZeneca: 750

The Riverside Research Park on the east side includes the National Cancer Institute's Frederick National Laboratory and Charles River Labs. Downtown has about 600 businesses and organizations with nearly 5,000 jobs. Wikipedia credits federal investment and the growth of the Washington metro area for much of the city's growth.

sections.h2: How does the Historic District affect selling or fixing up a house?
sections.html:
If your house is inside Downtown Frederick's historic district, exterior changes need approval from the city's Historic Preservation Commission before work begins. The commission's guidance says all exterior alterations require approval unless they are on a minor rehabilitation list.

Items the guide names include:

  • Sheds, fences, gates, walls and paving, including patios and driveways
  • Repair or replacement of doors and windows
  • Additions, porches, stoops, and outdoor HVAC or utility equipment
  • New lighting fixtures

Some projects are approved by Planning staff, while larger ones go to a Commission hearing with a sign posted at the site. The brochures do not define the exact district boundary, so call the city's Planning Department to find out whether your street is covered. For a seller, the trade-off is simple: fixing up a historic house before listing can take longer than you expect, and a buyer who plans to renovate will need to account for the review. Selling as is avoids starting any of that work yourself.

sections.h2: Does Carroll Creek or the weather create flood risk for a Frederick house?
sections.html:
Parts of Frederick have a documented flood history. Carroll Creek Park began in the late 1970s as a flood control project after floods in 1972 and 1976, and it now serves as a downtown park with an amphitheater and pedestrian bridges.

The climate is humid subtropical, with an average annual precipitation of 43.52 inches and average snowfall of 16.5 inches. Wikipedia lists a July mean daily maximum of 88.6 degrees F and a January mean daily minimum of 26.5 degrees F. The record high of 109 degrees F on July 10, 1936, is the highest ever recorded in Maryland. Heavy summer rain and winter freezes can mean basement moisture, gutter problems and roof wear, so those are the first places a buyer's inspector will look.

Check FEMA's flood map for your exact address and keep any flood insurance paperwork handy for the buyer.

sections.h2: How do I get around Frederick, and why does commute time matter?
sections.html:
Frederick sits on a junction of I-70, I-270, US 15, US 40 and US 340, with MD 80, MD 144 and MD 355 inside the area. Commuting to the Washington region is a major reason people buy here, so a house near a ramp or a MARC station may attract different buyers from one on a quiet street.

MARC commuter rail runs to Washington, D.C., express bus route 991 goes to Shady Grove Metro, and TransIT runs local buses. Frederick Municipal Airport (FDK) handles general aviation with a mile-long main runway. Schools come from Frederick County Public Schools, and higher education includes Frederick Community College, Hood College and a campus of Mount St. Mary's University.

sections.h2: What are the property tax and closing steps for a Frederick seller?
sections.html:
Frederick County mails annual and semi-annual tax bills in July, and they are posted online by July 1. Annual bills are due September 30, and semi-annual bills split into September 30 and December 31 installments. Interest begins on October 1 at 1% per month on unpaid balances.

Paying in July earns a 1% discount and paying in August earns a 0.5% discount. The county Treasury Department is at 30 N. Market St. and can be reached at 301-600-1111. The treasury page says each municipality levies its own tax and does not say who bills the City of Frederick portion, so ask the Treasury Department before closing.

The state reassessed Frederick County for January 1, 2026. Residential values rose 16.3% on average from January 1, 2023, and the increase is phased in evenly across three years. Check your latest SDAT notice if you are selling soon, because the new phase-in amount affects the tax proration at closing.

The legislative services table lists no county transfer tax for Frederick County and a recordation tax figure of $7.00, though the table does not spell out what unit that figure applies to. Ask your title company for the exact closing figures, along with the state's own transfer and recordation amounts.

sections.h2: Do Frederick landlords need a rental license?
sections.html:
The Board of Aldermen reportedly approved a rental licensing ordinance in 2022, but confirm the current status with the City of Frederick before relying on it. A local news report said owners of rental properties would need a license starting January 1, 2024, at a fee of $120.

The same report described inspections of at least 15% of units each year, a free first inspection, and fines up to $1,000 for operating unlicensed units. It did not say whether the mayor signed the measure. If you rent your house, call the city for the present rules, and ask whether any license or inspection items are open before you sign a sale contract.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Frederick usually face?
sections.html:
Frederick sellers commonly deal with one of three situations: an older downtown house with repairs and preservation rules, a rental that needs a license check, or a house in a family estate. A few other points come up repeatedly.

  • A deadline to close before a move for work.
  • A house with deferred maintenance after years of renting.
  • Back taxes, liens or an unpaid water bill that must be cleared at settlement.
  • Maryland's disclosure or disclaimer form, which most sellers of one-to-four unit homes must give the buyer.

faqs.q: Is Frederick a good place to sell a house quickly?
faqs.a: Demand is supported by Fort Detrick, the county school system and biomedical employers, but your timeline depends on the house's condition and price. A cash sale can shorten it because the buyer does not need lender approval.

faqs.q: When are Frederick County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Annual bills are due September 30, and semi-annual bills are due September 30 and December 31. Interest of 1% per month starts on October 1 for unpaid balances.

faqs.q: Do I need approval to repair my house in downtown Frederick?
faqs.a: If the house is in the historic district, exterior work generally needs Historic Preservation Commission approval unless it is on the minor rehabilitation list. Call the city Planning Department to check your address.

faqs.q: What is the combined property tax rate in the City of Frederick?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 combined rate in the legislative services table is $1.7134 per $100 of assessed value. The county-wide rate alone is $1.1100.

faqs.q: How much did Frederick assessments go up?
faqs.a: SDAT reports a 16.3% average residential increase in Frederick County from January 1, 2023 to January 1, 2026. Increases are phased in over three years.
